A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the North Sea oil boom was a major factor in the restructuring of employment and the economy of the North East of Scotland and that the effects of this boom have continued to be felt, albeit in a modified form, since the mid 1980s.
we have shown that there is no single model of the new economy, and that the nature of change is complex and diverse.
there are new forms of work in the North East, but that they are not as new, as different, or as pervasive, as is often assumed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the North Sea oil and gas industry has been an important factor in the development of the North East's economy, but it is not a panacea to its problems.
there is a need for more nuanced and context-sensitive analysis of new forms of work organisation and their implications for employment and skills.
the offshore construction industry has had an important impact in terms of the nature of the jobs and skills it has brought to the North-East of England.
